statement: Cellular production rates of EPS and other extracellular carbohydrates increase with specific growth rate.

scores.rationale: Snippet [1] directly states the stylized fact (cellular EPS/extracellular carbohydrate production rates increase with specific growth rate, citing source 38). Several DEB-based modeling papers (Livanou et al., LivaLaga2017) provide consistent supporting evidence: higher specific (per cell) carbohydrate release rates are observed in the exponential growth phase than the stationary phase ([2], [12], [14], [7]), aligning with the idea that production scales with growth rate. Snippet [4] (MarsTang2023) supports the mechanistic analog that extracellular enzyme production is proportional to specific growth rate. However, some snippets note maximum carbohydrate production at the transition/intermediate phase rather than strictly at peak growth, introducing minor nuance but not direct contradiction. Many remaining snippets are off-topic (cell size, C:N stoichiometry, rRNA/protein, maturity). Overall the evidence is moderate, with no contradicting findings, so the consensus direction is corroborative.
